input.quote: 14.5 Limitation of Liability. NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES OR LOST PROFITS ARISING FROM OR RELATING TO ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF ANY NOTICE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.
input.rationale: Section 14.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision and it contains no aggregate monetary cap: it is a mutual waiver of indirect/consequential, incidental, punitive damages and lost profits only, with carve-outs preserving indemnification under Sections 14.1/14.2 and damages for confidentiality (Article XI) and IP (Article X) breaches. Searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" and "in no event" surface no cap anywhere else (the only monetary limits are the $520,000,000 milestone ceiling in Article IX and the royalty offset floor), and Section 14.6 confirms insurance does not create a liability limit. Because no cap exists for either party, the clause fails even the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs) on the material "cap exists" term, leaving Sanofi's direct-damages exposure unlimited. The exclusion of indirect damages and the existing indemnity/confidentiality/IP carve-outs already meet the playbook on those points, so the redline is confined to inserting a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, extending the carve-outs to gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud, and confirming Sanofi's Article IX payment obligations are not capped damages. Note the exposure is symmetrical (RevMed is likewise uncapped), so this is a mutual fix rather than a one-sided walk-away item.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate monetary cap to Section 14.5 and extend the existing carve-outs to gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud, while confirming Sanofi's payment obligations sit outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.5 waives indirect damages but contains no monetary cap, so each Party's direct-damages exposure is unlimited; our position is a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality, IP, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud remain outside the cap, and Sanofi's payment obligations are not treated as capped damages.

ops.oldText: NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE INDEMNIFICATION RIGHTS OR OBLIGATIONS OF ANY PARTY UNDER SECTION 14.1 OR SECTION 14.2, OR DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO CONFIDENTIALITY UNDER ARTICLE XI OR INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY UNDER ARTICLE X.
ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY SANOFI TO REVMED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 14.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE FOLLOWING (THE "EXCLUDED CLAIMS"): THE INDEMNIFICATION RIGHTS OR OBLIGATIONS OF ANY PARTY UNDER SECTION 14.1 OR SECTION 14.2, OR DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS OBLIGATIONS RELATING TO CONFIDENTIALITY UNDER ARTICLE XI OR INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY UNDER ARTICLE X, OR A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD. FOR CLARITY, SANOFI'S OBLIGATION TO PAY AMOUNTS DUE UNDER ARTICLE IX SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THE FOREGOING CAP.
